CWE-798.impact: Anyone with repository access or retained Git history can recover the secret and use it outside the application.
CWE-798.remediation: Revoke and rotate the exposed value, remove it from current and historical commits, and load it from an approved secret manager.

CWE-200.impact: Tracked environment files can disclose credentials and operational configuration to every repository reader.
CWE-200.remediation: Remove the file from Git history, rotate all contained secrets, commit an example file with placeholders, and enforce secret scanning.

CWE-614.impact: A browser may send session tokens over an insecure channel or in a cross-site context, increasing token theft and request-forgery risk.
CWE-614.remediation: Set Secure and an explicit SameSite policy on authentication cookies; retain HttpOnly and use a bounded lifetime.

CWE-347.impact: Code may trust attacker-controlled token claims when a decoded value reaches an identity or authorization decision.
CWE-347.remediation: Verify the token signature, issuer, audience, use, and expiry before reading claims; pass only verified claims downstream.

CWE-918.impact: Attacker-controlled HTML rendered by a browser-backed PDF engine can cause server-side requests or active content execution.
CWE-918.remediation: Render from escaped structured fields, forbid remote resource loading, allowlist URL schemes and hosts, and isolate the renderer from internal networks.

default.impact: The identified behavior may weaken an application security boundary.
default.remediation: Remove the unsafe behavior and add a regression test for the affected trust boundary.
